subject: Dedicated GPU allocation for HelixAI — prioritization proposal
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@helixai.com>, Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv@helixai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU allocation for HelixAI — prioritization proposal

Hi Sara / Rajiv —

Thanks again for the call today. As promised I put together a short proposal for how we can map HelixAI's dedicated capacity request onto our current fleet while minimizing disruption for other high-priority customers. Key asks from your side I recorded: guaranteed 1200 rps token throughput during weekday peak windows (14:00-20:00 ET) for the next two quarters, and isolation for PII-heavy inference jobs.

Proposal highlights (attached full matrix):
- Reserve 8x A100-equivalent GPUs for HelixAI as a dedicated pool, backed by burst access up to 12 GPUs for 4 hours/day during peak release windows.
- Implement prefix KV-caching for warm models to reduce steady-state token cost.
- Canary period: 3-week ramp with a rollback/cutover SLA in our console.

Please confirm whether the above aligns with your timeline for the Nov 15 release. If you need a firmer SLA (99.9% availability for the reserved pool) we will need an addendum to the MAAP.

Attachment: capacity_request_v2.pdf (PDF)

Next steps: please confirm acceptance or list the non-negotiables by Friday so we can overlay this against existing reservations and provide a firm carve-out schedule.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Patel <sara@helixai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv@helixai.com>, procurement@helixai.com, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU allocation for HelixAI — prioritization proposal

Vivek —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. The Nov 15 date is firm for launch of our new chat assistant; we need the 1200 rps SLA during 14:00-20:00 ET and the PII isolation. If you cannot guarantee the exact GPU type, we need token-latency under 120ms p50 and clear escalation paths.

Procurement note: we can sign the MAAP addendum, but pricing and a penalty schedule for availability shortfalls must be in the SOW. I cc'd our procurement lead (procurement@helixai.com).

If you can get a provisional carve schedule in the next 48 hours, we'll route procurement and legal immediately.

— Sara
Sara Patel
VP Product — HelixAI
[Attachment: Helix_traffic_forecast_Q4.csv (CSV)]
From: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@helixai.com>, Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv@helixai.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Dedicated GPU allocation for HelixAI — prioritization proposal

Team / Sara —

Quick context from Sales: HelixAI is in late-stage procurement (deal DL-7821). They are a target expansion account for Q4 with strong reference potential. However, we have two concurrent commitments in the same region: OrionCloud renewal (SLA-exception committed last quarter) and an internal platform migration test window that consumes burst capacity evenings Wed–Fri.

Attached is a draft capacity decision matrix showing three options:
1) Full dedicated carve (8 GPUs reserved) — highest customer satisfaction, highest risk to renewals schedule.
2) Hybrid reserved + burst (4 reserved + 4 burst) — balances risk; requires strict throttling policy for burst preemption.
3) Time-windowed carve (8 GPUs but only guaranteed for 14:00-20:00 ET) — lowest continuous impact.

My recommendation: option 2 for the ramp. It gives Helix predictable baseline capacity while preserving scheduled renewals. We would accompany this with a canary for the Nov 15 go-live and a contractual burst SLA.

Attachment: capacity_decision_matrix.xlsx (Excel)

Neha
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara@helixai.com>, Rajiv Kapoor <rajiv@helixai.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T10:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU allocation for HelixAI — prioritization proposal

Thanks Neha —

Decision guidance from capacity ops: prioritize contractual renewals first (we have an SLA exception with OrionCloud that we committed to on record). That said, HelixAI is a strong candidate for hybrid carve if we can operationalize clear preemption rules. We should avoid a full hard reserve that blocks the rest of the fleet.

Action items I want tracked before we give Helix firm commitment:
- Vivek: run a short simulation of 14:00-20:00 ET traffic with option 2 to confirm latency tail behavior and KV-cache hit improvements. Deliver by EOD 11/06.
- Karthik: draft the burst preemption policy language (burstable window, notification SLA, penalty on missed notification).
- Neha: flag the required MAAP addendum clauses and estimated dollar impact for finance.

If the simulation looks clean, we sign off on the hybrid reserved + burst approach and present it to Helix with a canary schedule. For escalation, if Helix's production releases cause >20% impact to OrionCloud SLA during peak windows, we will activate manual arbitration and temporarily scale down bursts.

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success Ops — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU allocation for HelixAI — prioritization proposal

Laura / team —

Ran a quick capacity plan with ops and here's a conservative operational proposal that balances obligations:
- Phase 1 (Nov 15–Dec 15 canary): 4 reserved GPUs + 4 burstable GPUs (option 2). Burstable GPUs are from a reserved burst pool with 30-minute notification for preemption.
- Phase 2 (Dec 16–Jan 31): increase reserved to 6 GPUs if canary meets p50 latency <120ms and p95 <350ms.
- Fallback: during simultaneous peak conflicts, burst allocation will be throttled first; if impact persists >2 consecutive days, manual arbitration will be triggered (SUP-3456).

SLA language to propose for the MAAP addendum (draft bullets):
- Availability for reserved pool: 99.5% monthly.
- Burst availability best-effort with 2-min degrade notification and credit schedule tied to Helix's monthly invoice.
- Penalty cap: credits not to exceed 20% of monthly reserved fees.

Related links: HubSpot DL-7821, Jira SUP-3456 for arbitration.

I'll slot a short call with Sara/Rajiv tomorrow to confirm this plan and walk the burst preemption flow. Neha — please prepare the SOW with the penalty schedule so legal can review ASAP.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Helix_MAAP_signed.pdf (PDF)]
